title: Safe, programmable delivery to selected cells throughout the human brain

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a delivery platform that can carry therapeutic payloads to chosen cell types across the human brain, with predictable exposure and acceptable safety. “Programmable” means that the intended cells, regions and dose can be specified and reliably reached. Broad coverage and selectivity must work together: distributing a substance widely does not establish that it reaches the right cells, and reaching one selected cell population locally does not establish coverage throughout the brain.

As a design synthesis, the platform would combine four capabilities: broad anatomical reach, cell selection, controllable dosing and human safety. Its intended scope includes diverse therapeutic payloads rather than a single drug or disease. The supplied research frames blood–brain barrier restrictions and the invasiveness or limited reach of direct delivery as motivations, but the retained scientific material does not substantiate those background assertions in detail. They remain a rationale requiring documentation, rather than independently verified findings in this record.

significance.text: Conditional impact synthesis: a reliable way to deliver diverse therapies to selected central nervous system cells could address a delivery constraint shared by multiple neurological treatment programs. Its direct achievement would be controlled access to intended cells. This could make it possible to test therapeutic mechanisms in locations or cell populations that an existing delivery method cannot adequately reach, and could reduce the need to develop a separate delivery solution for every payload.

The downstream possibilities remain conditional. A successful platform could support gene regulation and other molecular treatments across several diseases, but each application would still need a suitable payload, a defensible biological target and independent evidence of benefit. Delivery cannot by itself establish that a disease mechanism is correct, replace lost tissue, restore learned function or reverse damage. Success with one payload, cell population or disease would also not establish that the platform works equally well for all others.

The platform analogy has practical limits. A reusable delivery method could simplify therapeutic development, but compatibility, exposure and safety would still need assessment for each materially different payload and use. The supplied evidence does not establish universal compatibility, predictable translation to living humans or the magnitude of any eventual clinical impact.

missing_breakthrough.text: The capability to be established is the integrated combination of broad coverage, selected-cell delivery, dose control and safety in living humans. These are separate requirements: transport into the central nervous system does not establish entry into the intended cells; cellular uptake does not establish that a payload reaches its site of action; and a biological effect in one region does not establish adequate distribution elsewhere. The supplied material does not determine whether this complete combination remains unavailable as of 1 November 2026.

Engineering synthesis: a convincing platform would need to preserve payload function during transport, deliver sufficient material to the intended intracellular or extracellular destination, and make exposure predictable across regions and patients. Cell selection would need to distinguish intended recipients from neighboring or peripheral cells. Dose control would need to connect the administered amount to the amount and duration of active payload at the target, rather than relying only on total brain-associated material.

Further design barriers include measuring uneven distribution, identifying off-target exposure, assessing immune effects and establishing whether repeat administration remains effective and tolerable when required. The delivery method must also accommodate meaningful differences among payloads without assuming that success with an oligonucleotide transfers to every other therapeutic class. These are proposed requirements derived from the concept, not findings demonstrated by the supplied correction notice.

current_state.text: The reconciled research attributes to Wang and colleagues a report published on 25 November 2024 describing a blood–brain-barrier-crossing conjugate, oligonucleotide delivery and gene silencing in mice, an ALS mouse model and tested human brain tissue. Those experimental details remain attributed reports here: the retained PubMed artifact contains only a cookie-access message, so the supplied review could not assess the abstract, methods or results. The earlier statement that the abstract was inspected is therefore not supported by the retained copy. This access limitation does not establish that the reported findings are false.

The separately verified author correction, published online on 4 March 2025, identifies chirality errors in the depicted structures of MK-0752 and its derivatives BCC7, BCC8, BCC9 and BCC10. It identifies Figures 1a and 2a and the Supplementary Information as affected and states that the structures were amended. According to the supplied review, the complete correction was available for assessment. It substantiates the structural amendments but does not supply enough experimental detail to evaluate the reported delivery or gene-silencing findings.

Even if the experimental account in the reconciled research is accurate, results in mice and tested human brain tissue would not by themselves establish programmable delivery throughout the brain of a living patient. Human tissue experiments and treatment in living humans have different evidentiary scope. The supplied account does not establish the tissue preparation, quantitative delivery efficiency, regional coverage, cell selectivity, therapeutic exposure or human safety needed to assess the full platform.

The available record establishes a dated publication and a subsequent structural correction, but it does not establish the field’s status as of 1 November 2026. The supplied search record for that later cutoff is empty. Consequently, neither continued absence nor subsequent achievement of the integrated platform can be inferred from these materials.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: prespecify intended cell types and brain regions, then independently measure whether active payload reaches those targets at exposures justified for the intended treatment. Measurements should distinguish anatomical distribution, cell uptake and functional target engagement. A demonstration of the title’s broad scope would need to examine geographically distributed regions and explicitly report missed regions and uneven delivery. Finite testing could establish the breadth demonstrated under defined conditions, not literal access to every cell or universal performance.
completion_criteria.label: Active payload reaches prespecified brain targets at treatment-justified exposures

completion_criteria.text: Proposed versatility and reproducibility criteria: demonstrate delivery using more than one materially different payload type and across multiple neurological conditions. Independent replication, reproducible manufacturing and consistent exposure across relevant patient variation would strengthen the case for a platform. Payloads, cell populations, disease states and administration routes outside the tested range should remain explicit boundaries of the claim.
completion_criteria.label: Delivery supports multiple materially different payload types across neurological conditions

completion_criteria.text: Proposed clinical criteria: controlled trials should establish target engagement, clinically meaningful benefit and acceptable off-target and immune effects for the applications being claimed. Therapeutic exposure, relevant regions, acceptable adverse effects and follow-up duration need condition-specific definitions set before evaluation. Where repeated treatment is intended, evidence should address repeat-dose performance and tolerability. These are proposed criteria for convincing evidence, not established consensus thresholds; clinical benefit would validate particular applications alongside the broader delivery capability.
completion_criteria.label: Controlled trials establish target engagement, clinical benefit and acceptable safety

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: NRL-09, preventing Alzheimer’s dementia; NRL-11, halting established Alzheimer’s disease and restoring function; and NRL-15, treating shared mechanisms of neurodegeneration, could use selected-cell delivery as an enabling technology. NRL-10 concerns getting a payload to its destination. The other concepts require evidence about disease mechanisms, intervention timing and outcomes that successful delivery alone cannot provide.

NRL-12, immune control and remyelination in multiple sclerosis; NRL-13, protection during acute ischemic stroke; NRL-14, durable seizure freedom; and NRL-18, interrupting the disease process associated with chronic traumatic encephalopathy, are potential application areas. Their overlap is the possible need to reach relevant cells. Their distinct requirements include immune regulation, tissue protection, seizure control and identification of a treatable disease process, respectively. None follows automatically from delivery performance.

NRL-05, spinal cord regeneration; NRL-06, replacement of lost brain tissue while preserving learned function; and NRL-16, biological repair of the visual pathway, overlap with delivery through possible transport of repair-promoting interventions. They additionally require functional reconstruction and integration. Spinal cord delivery also extends beyond the brain-specific coverage named in NRL-10 and would need its own demonstration.

NRL-03, whole-brain cellular-resolution recording, and NRL-04, reading and selectively repairing memory traces, could potentially use delivery to introduce molecular probes or interventions. Recording activity, identifying a specific memory trace and repairing it remain separate capabilities. Likewise, NRL-01, a causal theory of consciousness, and NRL-02, a predictive theory of neural circuit computation, concern explanatory and predictive understanding; delivery could support experiments without establishing either theory.

NRL-07, dependable neural communication for profound paralysis; NRL-08, a visual-cortex prosthesis; and NRL-17, a bidirectional interface for movement and sensation, concern functional communication with neural systems. Selected-cell delivery might assist particular implementations, but it does not itself supply reliable signal decoding, stimulation, sensory encoding or durable interface performance. These remain distinct roster entries.

brief.title: Safe delivery of treatments to chosen brain cells
possible: People with neurological diseases could receive treatments that reach chosen cell types across the brain at predictable doses. Researchers could specify which cells and regions receive a treatment, with acceptable safety.
Researchers could test treatments in cells they cannot adequately reach today. The same delivery system could carry different kinds of therapeutic material.
why: Getting a treatment to its intended cells is a shared obstacle across neurological treatment programs. A reusable delivery system could reduce the need to solve that problem separately for each treatment.

sources.showed: They delivered oligonucleotides, short strands of genetic material, across the blood–brain barrier, which restricts passage from blood into the brain. They reduced gene activity in mice and tested human brain tissue.
sources.quote: Intravenous administration of a BCC10-oligonucleotide conjugate demonstrated effective transportation of the oligonucleotide across the BBB and gene silencing in wild-type mice, human brain tissues and an amyotrophic lateral sclerosis mouse model.
sources.cited_for: The study supports delivery of genetic material and reduction of gene activity in experimental settings.
sources.not_established: It does not establish safe, predictable delivery to selected cells throughout a living human brain.

sources.showed: The authors corrected errors in drawings of the molecules' spatial arrangement in the original study.
sources.cited_for: The correction establishes that molecular structure drawings needed amendment.
sources.not_established: The correction does not establish whether the drawing errors affect interpretation of the experimental results.

shown: Chang Wang and colleagues demonstrated delivery of genetic material and reduced gene activity in mice, including a model of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, and in tested human brain tissue. This work does not demonstrate delivery throughout the brain of a living person.
missing: Active treatment still needs to reach chosen cells across widely separated brain regions in living humans.
The administered dose still needs to predict how much active treatment reaches each target and how long it lasts.
A reusable system still needs to deliver materially different treatments across neurological conditions.
Controlled human trials still need to establish benefit, acceptable safety and tolerability of repeated treatment where needed.

milestones.label: Active treatment reaches specified brain cells at useful doses
milestones.explanation: Measurements would have to show active treatment reaching specified cells across widely separated brain regions at treatment-justified amounts. This would establish useful delivery and reveal missed targets.

milestones.label: Delivery works across different treatments and neurological conditions
milestones.explanation: Studies would have to demonstrate delivery of materially different therapeutic materials across neurological conditions. Reproducible results would support a reusable system.

milestones.label: Controlled trials establish benefit and acceptable safety
milestones.explanation: Controlled trials would have to show the treatment acting on its intended target, meaningful clinical benefit and acceptable safety. This would validate particular uses, including repeated treatment where intended.

uncertain: The amount of treatment needed, acceptable unevenness in delivery and required safety follow-up depend on the application.
It remains unclear whether the corrected molecular drawings change interpretation of the experimental results.
Success with a particular treatment or cell population may not transfer to others.

page.title: Brain-wide cell-type-specific delivery of therapeutics
page.definition: A therapeutic payload acts preferentially in a specified cell population across the regions of the living human brain where those cells occur. Specificity is the fraction of cells showing activity that belong to the intended type. Coverage is the fraction of that type showing activity in each region. Target-cell exposure is related to the administered dose, and safety is established for the tested use. Onasemnogene abeparvovec illustrates the distinction: postmortem samples showed protein expression in both brain neurons and glia, as well as in peripheral tissues.

goal.need: When disease affects one cell population across several brain regions, a medicine must reach those cells while limiting its effects on surrounding tissue. Dravet syndrome illustrates the need. In a 2016 survey of 584 caregivers, fewer than 10% of patients had gone three months without seizures despite care that generally followed treatment guidelines. For children whose disease results from loss of SCN1A function, restoring that function in inhibitory neurons across affected circuits could reduce seizures while limiting unintended changes in excitatory neurons.

completion.title: A human study verifies brain-wide delivery to a specified cell type within its exposure and safety limits.
completion.criterion: A registered human study meets prespecified endpoints for functional delivery of a specified payload to its intended cell population across the brain, the relationship between administered dose and target-cell exposure, and safety over the protocol's follow-up period. Regional and cellular measurements must distinguish intended activity from activity in other brain cells and peripheral tissues. The protocol must define coverage, selectivity, exposure limits and adverse-event limits before treatment. Achievement establishes the tested payload, target population and regimen.
completion.set_by: Atlas; no external completion criterion for the integrated human capability was found.
completion.basis: Searches covered NIH BRAIN Armamentarium calls, NIH TARGETED prize rules, ARPA-H CT-NEURO objectives, FDA gene-therapy guidance and human trial records. No joint human threshold for brain-wide coverage, cell specificity, dose–exposure control and safety was found. This test confines achievement to a specified application and uses protocol-defined limits; it does not establish compatibility with arbitrary payloads or cell types.

milestones.title: An animal study confirms delivery to the intended brain site or cell population.
milestones.criterion: An in vivo proof-of-concept study confirms that the investigational product reaches its prespecified brain target by the proposed route. For an anatomical target, the study identifies the brain site reached. For a cellular target, it identifies the cells reached.
milestones.set_by: FDA, Preclinical Assessment of Investigational Cellular and Gene Therapy Products, section III.B.4; nonbinding guidance for cellular and gene therapies.
milestones.threshold_quote: Optimization of the ROA and confirmation that the CGT product reaches the target anatomic site/tissue/cell.

milestones.title: Preclinical studies identify an active dose range and support a brain therapy's initial human dose.
milestones.criterion: Preclinical studies identify a biologically active dose range and support the proposed initial human dose, dose-escalation schedule and route of administration. They characterize distribution to target and non-target tissues and identify potential toxicities and the measures needed for clinical monitoring.
milestones.set_by: FDA, Human Gene Therapy for Neurodegenerative Diseases, section III; these recommendations were written for neurodegenerative disease products.
milestones.threshold_quote: identification of a biologically active dose range;

The application takes effect 30 days after FDA receives it unless FDA places the investigation on clinical hold, or earlier if FDA notifies the sponsor that the investigation may begin.
milestones.set_by: FDA, 21 CFR 312.40(b) and (d); the authorization criterion stated here is specific to the United States.
milestones.threshold_quote: An investigator may not administer an investigational new drug to human subjects until the IND goes into effect under paragraph (b) of this section.

milestones.title: ENDEAVOR Part 1 demonstrates safety and preliminary efficacy sufficient for controlled testing of ETX101.
milestones.criterion: For ETX101 in SCN1A-positive Dravet syndrome, the Part 1 dose-escalation study must demonstrate safety and preliminary efficacy sufficient to proceed to controlled testing in Part 2. The sponsor’s published progression rule gives no numerical cutoff for either outcome.
milestones.set_by: Encoded Therapeutics, published ENDEAVOR Part 1-to-Part 2 progression rule for ETX101 in SCN1A-positive Dravet syndrome
milestones.threshold_quote: Part 2 is planned following demonstration of safety and efficacy in ENDEAVOR Part 1.

milestones.title: An animal study measures target-cell specificity and coverage across the brain.
milestones.criterion: For a reagent intended for near-global brain delivery, measure specificity and coverage at the whole-brain level. Across brain regions, determine what fraction of cells showing payload activity belong to the intended type and what fraction of cells of that type show activity. The NIH programme sets a measurement objective without a universal percentage cutoff.
milestones.set_by: NIH BRAIN Initiative, RFA-MH-25-100, Validation of Reagent Specificity and Efficiency
milestones.threshold_quote: Measures of specificity and efficiency at the whole brain level are a priority for reagents designed for near global brain delivery.

not_found: Public ENDEAVOR material did not provide a numerical safety-and-efficacy rule for progression to Part 2.
Regional, cell-resolved human distribution measurements establishing brain-wide selectivity for ETX101 were not found.
No regulator or professional society statement disputing the value or feasibility of brain-wide cell-type-specific therapeutic delivery was found.

results.quote: All doses of CAP-002 surpass this efficacy threshold in NHPs.

results.finding: In mice (4 per group), the GABA-selective reporter was expressed in 58.9% of GAD67-positive cells in sampled brain sections.
results.detail: The cellular percentages came from an EGFP reporter using the same regulatory element. ETX101's cell-resolved activity was tested in mouse cortex.
results.quote: AAV9-RE GABA -EGFP drove EGFP expression in 58.9% ± 14.4% GAD67-positive cells, 67.2% ± 18.7% PV-positive cells, and 82.0% ± 14.3% SST-positive cells

results.finding: In 4 ETX101-treated juvenile macaques, intracerebroventricular doses up to 8.0 × 10¹³ vector genomes per animal were tolerated.
results.detail: The pilot pooled the two macaque dose groups for distribution and expression analyses because it found no systematic differences. Mouse efficacy experiments used different endpoints, and the paper cautions that doses from some experiments were not directly comparable.
results.quote: AAV9-RE GABA -eTF SCN1A  was well tolerated with no adverse events occurring during administration and no detectable changes in clinical observations, body weight, or body temperature during the 28-day study.

results.finding: In Dravet-model mice (n=4), cortical GABAergic interneurons expressing the ETX101 transgene had about 30% more SCN1A RNA than those without detectable transgene RNA.
results.quote: GABAergic neurons containing eTF SCN1A  transcript expressed ∼30% more  SCN1A  than GABAergic cells that lacked eTF SCN1A  ( Fig. 3C ; blue panel, average TPK 0.69 vs. 0.54;  p  < 0.001; one-sided rank-sum test).

results.finding: In mice given the targeted EGFP reporter (n=4 per group), 58.9% of GAD67-positive cells in sampled brain sections expressed EGFP.
results.detail: The coverage estimate comes from an EGFP reporter using the ETX101 regulatory element. The regional macaque assays lacked cell-level resolution.
results.quote: At a dose level of 2.0E10 vg per animal, AAV9-RE GABA -EGFP drove EGFP expression in 58.9% ± 14.4% GAD67-positive cells, 67.2% ± 18.7% PV-positive cells, and 82.0% ± 14.3% SST-positive cells, whereas AAV9-CBA-EGFP exhibited significantly lower expression coverage ( Fig. 2D ).

results.finding: In a pilot study of juvenile macaques (n=4 treated, 2 controls), ETX101 was tolerated at doses up to 8.0×10^13 vector genomes per animal.
results.detail: The pilot was non-GLP. The two active dose groups were pooled for biodistribution analysis after the authors observed no systematic differences in brain vector copy number or transgene RNA.
results.quote: ICV-administered doses of AAV9-RE GABA -eTF SCN1A  at up to 8E13 vector genomes (vg) per animal were well tolerated, with no detectable changes in clinical observations, no adverse findings in histopathology, and no dorsal root ganglion (DRG)-related toxicity.

results.finding: In C57BL/6J mice (n = 3 per group), ~95% of AAV-X1-transduced cells in sampled cortex, hippocampus, and thalamus were GLUT1+.
results.detail: The study also imaged whole rat brains after AAV-X1.1 delivery, but the text reports qualitative reporter distribution and endothelial overlap without whole-brain estimates of either fraction.
results.quote: ~95% of the cells transduced by AAV-X1 were GLUT1+.

results.finding: After intravenous AAV-9P31 in four mice, 39.4% of GFP-positive cortical cells were microglia.
results.detail: Figure 7 reports specificity and coverage in the cerebrum, cerebellum, hippocampus, striatum, thalamus, olfactory bulb, and pons. Vascular endothelial cells accounted for most off-target GFP expression.

Quantification of the immunohistochemistry showed that the specificity of GFP expression 
for microglia in the cerebral cortex was approximately 40% (39.4 ± 8.9%, n = 4 mice).

results.finding: GS-100 pharmacology in 63 rats and toxicology in rats and macaques supported a first-in-human starting dose of 4e14 vector genomes per person.

definition = "A therapeutic payload acts preferentially in a specified cell population across the regions of the living human brain where those cells occur. Specificity is the fraction of cells showing activity that belong to the intended type. Coverage is the fraction of that type showing activity in each region. Target-cell exposure is related to the administered dose, and safety is established for the tested use. Onasemnogene abeparvovec illustrates the distinction: postmortem samples showed protein expression in both brain neurons and glia, as well as in peripheral tissues.". Reason: The definition explains selectivity but leaves out the separate question of how many intended cells respond in each region.

goal.need = "When disease affects one cell population across several brain regions, a medicine must reach those cells while limiting its effects on surrounding tissue. Dravet syndrome illustrates the need. In a 2016 survey of 584 caregivers, fewer than 10% of patients had gone three months without seizures despite care that generally followed treatment guidelines. For children whose disease results from loss of SCN1A function, restoring that function in inhibitory neurons across affected circuits could reduce seizures while limiting unintended changes in excitatory neurons.". Reason: The global disease count and mouse cell-type count do not quantify the treatment problem or explain why patients would benefit from cell selectivity.

add statement by National Institutes of Health, Targeted Genome Editor Delivery Challenge, Target Area 2, 2023: "demonstrate delivery and editing in a substantial proportion of clinically relevant cell types in the brain.". Reason: The NIH challenge names a preclinical delivery goal that is more specific about the payload, the blood–brain barrier and the target cells than either existing statement.

edit m1: title = "An animal study confirms delivery to the intended brain site or cell population."; criterion = "An in vivo proof-of-concept study confirms that the investigational product reaches its prespecified brain target by the proposed route. For an anatomical target, the study identifies the brain site reached. For a cellular target, it identifies the cells reached."; threshold_quote = "Optimization of the ROA and confirmation that the CGT product reaches the target anatomic site/tissue/cell."; threshold_ref = 5; refs = [5]. Reason: The title requires confirmation in target cells even though the FDA guidance also accepts an anatomical target, and the criterion mixes that test with individual study results.

add milestone after m1: "An animal study measures target-cell specificity and coverage across the brain.". Reason: The sequence jumps from delivery at one target to clinical dose selection without measuring whether cell selectivity and coverage extend across the brain.

edit m2: criterion = "Preclinical studies identify a biologically active dose range and support the proposed initial human dose, dose-escalation schedule and route of administration.
